drafts.title: Honda Prologue Touring AWD still leases like a mid-$400s payment. Amortize the due.
drafts.window: ~3 PM MT Monday (afternoon OK). Soft-pedal defaulting to 11-2.
drafts.angle: Electrek factory table (updated Sep 13): 2026 Prologue AWD Touring about $279/mo for 36 months with $5,099 due (effective ~$413 before tax), expires ~Nov 2, 2026. Soft-pedal Sat Uncharted / Sun Solterra / Sun Mach-E twins by stressing Honda badge + Touring equipment + longer expire window. Kitchen-table: family crossover payment math without rehashing Subaru/Ford.
bullets: Electrek manufacturer table (~Sep 13, 2026): Honda Prologue AWD Touring ~$279/mo, 36 mo, $5,099 due, 10,000 mi/yr; avg monthly cost ~$413; MSRP ~$48,495; expires ~Nov 2, 2026.
Same Electrek dealer table: McGovern Honda Prologue EX AWD advertised ~$179/mo / avg ~$279 with ~$3,773 due (verify local and VIN).
CarsDirect earlier Sep Prologue EX AWD loyalty path showed ~$259/mo / $4,599 due (effective ~$387) but that national line listed exp ~Sep 8, 2026. Prefer the still-open factory Touring line above.
Soft-pedal Sat Uncharted $405/$1,415 and Sun Solterra $415/$1,415 if still unposted; different brand and equipment story.
Soft-pedal Fri EV6 / Fri Niro twins.
drafts.body:
A Prologue lease ad that only shows the monthly is half a conversation.

Electrek's factory line still shows a 2026 Touring AWD around $279 a month for 36 months with about $5,099 due. Average that drive-off and you are nearer $410 a month before tax. That is a different sticky-note than a $405 Subaru with a tiny due, and a different sticky-note than a Mach-E Select with a bigger due.

US kitchen-table take for a 40-year-old shopping a family crossover, or a 58-year-old who wants a simple payment stack:

1) Ask for the out-the-door sheet on the exact Touring VIN, not a website monthly.
2) Divide due-at-signing by months, then add the payment. That is your real lease number.
3) Quote insurance on that VIN before you sign.
4) Map weekday Level 2 at home, work, or a real apartment plan if you rent.
5) Confirm miles/year. A 10,000-mile line can sting if you actually drive more.

35-54 line: Premium timelines save "amortize the due" math. This is a save-and-repost payment post.

55+ line: a mid-$400s effective lease only helps if insurance and the plug plan keep your independence.

Up to 20% bill savings for standard subscribers; 50% for income-qualified Illinois Shines path. First-year estimated savings ~$163,000 combined: ~$98,000 to residential subscribers; ~$65,000+ to OSF Saint Anthony Medical Center.

drafts.body:
You do not need a roof to get a solar line on your bill.

Rockford just marked one year on a 6.2 MW community solar farm with about 20,000 panels. Nearly 690 households plugged into ComEd credits. Year one: about $98,000 saved on residential bills, plus more than $65,000 for the local hospital. Standard subscribers save up to 20%. Income-qualified paths can cut half the bill.

US kitchen-table take for a renter, a shaded roof, or a 60-year-old who does not want a 25-year roof contract:

1) Ask your utility if community solar subscriptions are open in your territory.
2) Read the bill-credit percent and the exit terms before you sign.
3) Compare that credit to your last 12 months of electric spend.
4) If a salesman pushes rooftop only, ask about shared solar first.
5) Keep politics out of it. This is a bill tool.

35-54 line: "year-one dollar proof" is a Premium save for renters and owners.

55+ line: bill credits without a roof loan keep independence simpler.

drafts.title: IONNA just cleared 1,500 fast stalls. The household number is the kWh price.
drafts.window: ~3 PM MT Monday (afternoon OK). Soft-pedal defaulting to 11-2.
drafts.angle: InsideEVs/AFDC Sep 12: IONNA at 1,526 DC stalls across 178 US locations (+50% stalls since late March). Sep 19 Hey Durham: 177 stations running, 80 under construction. Avg price ~$0.38/kWh vs industry ~$0.56/kWh. Soft-pedal Fri Red E Go LIVE and Wed NYC It's Electric LIVE by stressing national network math and road-trip independence for families already driving EVs.
bullets: AFDC via InsideEVs (Sep 12, 2026): IONNA 1,526 stalls at 178 locations; had ~1,000 stalls late March 2026 (+~500 / ~50% in under six months).
Hey Durham (Sep 19, 2026): 177 stations running as of Sep 17; 80 under construction; several hundred in planning; ~30 states; goal ~30,000 ports by 2030.
Same InsideEVs: Circle K sites being upgraded with up to 400 kW chargers; plans to assume ~85 Circle K sites and build 265+ more at select Circle K locations.
DCFC Tracker note in same piece: IONNA avg ~$0.38/kWh vs industry avg ~$0.56/kWh; ~36% of stalls NACS (~548); JD Power 2026 DC fast top score 807/1000.
Soft-pedal Fri Red E Go plug-n-go LIVE and Tue home ~$11 vs IONNA ~$0.39/kWh LIVE twin.
drafts.body:
Road-trip anxiety is a bill and a map problem, not a bumper-sticker problem.

IONNA just crossed about 1,500 fast-charging stalls at nearly 180 US sites. That is roughly 50% more stalls than late March. The household number that matters on a Tuesday afternoon: about $0.38 per kWh average versus an industry average near $0.56. Founding automakers are still building even after tax-credit chaos.

US kitchen-table take for a 42-year-old with a family EV, or a 60-year-old who wants one reliable highway plan:

1) Check the IONNA map for your next three road corridors before you buy or lease.
2) Compare the app's kWh price to the last highway charger you used.
3) Ask if your brand has a member discount (many founding brands do 10-20%).
4) Pair highway fast charge with cheap overnight Level 2 at home or work. Do not live on DC only.
5) Soft-pedal "charger deserts" takes without checking the live map for your ZIP.

35-54 line: "$0.38 vs $0.56" is a Premium save for road-trip households.

55+ line: a reliable highway plug is independence, not a hobby.
